copy.assessment: On PTRACE-GID, EXCH, COPY, complete SCAN-GATE/SCAN-W, credential closure and the stated trusted root/kernel, the descriptor-confined creates, explicit writes and root exchanges protect the fresh destination inodes at each explicit mutation. Generic ptrace documentation supports the UID/GID prerequisite but is not installed-host evidence. K5's universal every-frame-mutation claim is false for source read side effects; exact attribute reproduction and source-read compatibility are also conditional. Root exchange changes admitted recipe-parent metadata, contradicting the immutable-after-M8 assertion.

in_place.assessment: K1 is an explicit conjunction, not an original acceptance predicate. The parent walk makes the route decision and the child rechecks entry ownership, effective write bits and device, tests leases on walk-matched file descriptors, compares all admitted leaf keys, and repeats credential scans after SPAWN_OK and before spawn. This is the right stated final-pass placement. Sufficiency remains conditional: L1, K-PERM, credential closure and a genuinely joint M-QUIESCENT state are unestablished. st_dev equality establishes device equality, not absence of every mount boundary; whole-population scan completeness and correspondence to a common quiescent instant are not specified by S1-S6.

k8.assessment: An access-time inode update caused by the frame's read is a frame-caused filesystem mutation; exclusion from stat_key is not a custody exception. A foreign-owned single-link source may have its sole current name outside T when the retained source descriptor is read. K8 expressly allows foreign-owned source reads without O_NOATIME and admits possible outside names. Directory enumeration also needs an explicit read-side-effect treatment. The 'one place only' statement omits the inherited proof-report read.
